Original Requirements: Build the Volopa OOP (Out-of-Pocket) Expenses API System covering User Management, Pocket Expense CSV Batch Upload, and Single Expense Data Capturing with role-based access control, CSV validation, and FX conversion capabilities.
Product Goals: Implement secure role-based permission system with delegation capabilities
Enable efficient CSV bulk upload with comprehensive validation
Provide real-time FX conversion with dated rates and client commission
Ensure seamless approval workflow for expense management
Deliver consistent RESTful API with proper error handling
Support flexible expense source configuration per client
Maintain audit trail for all permission changes and expense operations
Optimize performance with caching and queue-based processing
User Stories: As a Primary Administrator, I want to manage all users' expenses and grant management rights to other administrators
As an Administrator, I want to upload CSV files with up to 200 expense records and see validation results immediately
As an Administrator with management rights, I want to approve/reject expenses for users under my management
As a Business User, I want to create single expense entries with automatic FX conversion based on my wallet currency
As a Card User, I want to track my out-of-pocket expenses with flexible metadata and custom sources
As any user, I want to see real-time converted amounts when entering expenses in foreign currencies
As an Administrator, I want to download CSV error reports when bulk upload validation fails
As a user, I want to receive notifications when my expenses are approved or rejected
As a Primary Admin, I want to configure custom expense sources for my organization
As any user, I want to view my expense history with filtering and search capabilities
Competitive Analysis: Expensify: Strong mobile app, receipt scanning, but complex pricing tiers
Concur SAP: Enterprise-focused, extensive integrations, but heavy UI and high cost
Zoho Expense: Good small business features, affordable, but limited customization
Rydoo: Modern UI, good mobile experience, but limited CSV bulk operations
Chrome River: Strong approval workflows, but outdated interface
Certify (Emburse): Good reporting, but weak API documentation
ExpensePoint: Simple interface, basic features, but lacks advanced permission management

Requirement Analysis: The system requires a sophisticated three-tier architecture: (1) User Management with hierarchical permissions and delegation capabilities through user_feature_permission table, (2) CSV Batch Upload with synchronous all-or-nothing validation for maximum 200 rows with comprehensive error reporting, and (3) Single Expense Management with real-time FX conversion using dated rates and client commission adjustments. Key technical challenges include maintaining ACID compliance during bulk operations, implementing efficient permission checks at every API endpoint, and providing seamless FX conversion with 30-day lookback functionality. The system must handle multiple user roles (Primary Administrator, Administrator, Business User, Card User) with granular permissions that can be delegated and revoked. Performance optimization through caching reference data, queue-based background processing, and proper database indexing is critical for scalability.
Requirement Pool: Implement OAuth2-protected RESTful API endpoints with role-based access control via user_feature_permission table
Develop CSV batch upload with synchronous validation for max 200 rows using all-or-nothing transaction logic
Create real-time FX conversion system with dated rates, 30-day lookback, and client commission calculations
Build comprehensive permission delegation system allowing Primary Admins to grant management rights to Administrators
Implement approval workflow for expense management with status transitions and notification system
UI Design draft: API-first design with JSON responses using Laravel API Resources. Main endpoints include: /api/expenses (CRUD operations), /api/uploads/pocket-expense/csv (bulk upload), /api/users/permissions (permission management), /api/fx-conversion (real-time FX rates). Each endpoint returns consistent JSON structure with proper HTTP status codes (200, 201, 204, 422). Error responses include structured validation errors with field-level details. CSV upload errors provide line-by-line validation results with downloadable error reports. Authentication handled via Oauth2UserClient middleware. Response caching for reference data (currencies, expense types, countries). Queue-based background processing for large CSV operations with status tracking.
